title: Ephemeral memoization for short-lived sessions - scratchpad
body:
Context / one-liner:
Small, chatty sessions (10–50 user turns) account for a disproportionate number of short spikes and replays. Full KV cache warmup and full-session persistence are expensive and often unnecessary. Idea: keep lightweight, per-session micro-snapshots (ephemeral memoization) that let clients resume or re-hydrate a partial context quickly without paying for the full persistent session overhead.

Why this feels important:
- Many customers use sessions for quick Q&A, step-by-step guides, or short transactions where only the last N turns matter.
- Warmup latency / token cost for repeated short sessions kills UX and increases per-turn cost.
- Dedicated persistence (DBs, S3) is overkill for ephemeral scenarios; we can optimize for speed + minimal storage.

Primary goal:
- Reduce average latency and token cost for short-lived session resumes by ~30% while keeping memory and storage overhead negligible.
- Provide a simple API for clients to snapshot/restore lightweight state and an internal heuristic to auto-snapshot hot sessions.

Success metrics (initial):
- P99 resume latency for sessions <= 50 turns drops by >= 25%
- Tokens consumed during resume reduced by >= 20% across pilot customers
- Incremental storage per active ephemeral snapshot < 2 KB on average
- No increase in error rate or hallucination score on eval prompts (sanity checks)

User stories / acceptance:
- As a web app dev, I want to call snapshot(session_id, hint) before redirecting the user so resuming the conversation is instant.
  - AC: snapshot returns a small snapshot_id; restore(snapshot_id) rehydrates the session and subsequent calls behave identically (within tolerance).
- As a product manager, I want the platform to auto-capture a memo for sessions with repeated short resumes so we don't rely on clients to opt-in.
  - AC: auto-snapshots created only for sessions that resume > 2x within 10 minutes and are < 60 turns.
- As an infra engineer, I want snapshots to be garbage-collected after TTL and respect privacy (no long-term PII storage).
  - AC: snapshots expire default 1 hour; configurable per-tenant with max 24 hours.

Design notes / constraints:
- Snapshot contents: compressed KV deltas (last k tokens + model decoder KV pointers), a lightweight instruction summary (first system turn hash), and a deterministic reconstruction hint. Not full parameter state.
- Store snapshots in a fast in-memory tier (memstore) with optional spillover to encrypted S3 for longer TTLs in Dedicated/Private.
- Snapshots should be model-agnostic where possible; include model id + tokenizer version to validate compatibility on restore.
- Avoid storing raw user messages beyond last k turns; prefer hashed pointers plus redaction flags.

API sketch (rough):
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/snapshot  -> { snapshot_id, size_bytes, ttl_seconds }
POST /v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/restore -> { session_id, restored: true }
GET /v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id} -> metadata (owner, created_at, model_id, turns_included)

Operational heuristics / auto policies:
- Auto-snapshot when: session length < 60 AND resume_count >= 2 in sliding 10m window AND average turn token count < 128.
- Eviction order: LRU of snapshot access, with priority to snapshots pinned by explicit client snapshot calls.
- Fallback: if snapshot restore fails (model mismatch, corruption), fallback to normal cold start with graceful notification to caller and automatic telemetry entry.

Experiments to run (MVP):
1) Pilot with 3 internal product customers (chat widgets) for 4 weeks: measure resume latency & token delta.
2) Controlled A/B on hosted runtime where 10% of eligible sessions get auto-snapshots. Compare UX metrics and cost.
3) Synthetic test harness: run 50k resume attempts across model variants to profile failure rates and size distribution.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Snapshot-based restores cause subtle context drift (missing environment state) -> Mitigate: include deterministic turn-hash verification, add safety net evaluation set for each model to check for regression.
- Risk: Storage/GDPR exposure -> Mitigate: default expiry short; redaction, KMS encryption; require enterprise opt-in for longer retention.
- Risk: Snapshot storm on scale -> Mitigate: rate-limit snapshot creation per org and global memstore quota, spillover to cold store.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- What is the minimal representation that gives >95% behavioral parity for N=6 last turns? (run decode fidelity bench)
- How to represent plugin/tool state between snapshots (tool outputs, external actions)? Probably mark as non-serializable and require explicit client checkpointing.
- Billing: snapshot RESTores should not double-bill tokens; need clear pricing model (cheap restore call + normal token billing on subsequent generation).
- UX: should Console surface live snapshot list per session? priority: low.

Implementation sketch for MVP (engineering notes):
- Add snapshot manager service in serving-runtime that captures K/V deltas at end-of-turn flush. Store a compressed proto blob + metadata.
- Expose lightweight API on Redwood API gateway; auth same as sessions.
- Restore path: allocate ephemeral session with pre-warmed KV cache from blob then attach to existing routing. Restore should be under 100ms for in-memory hits.

Telemetry we should add:
- snapshot.create, snapshot.restore, snapshot.expire, snapshot.restore_failure{reason}, snapshot.auto_created boolean, snapshot.size_bytes, snapshot.model_mismatch boolean

Example mock client flow (notes):
- client: POST /sessions/abcd/turn -> user types then client does POST /sessions/abcd/snapshot?hint=boarding
- later: GET /snapshots/xyz/restore -> server returns 200 and a new active session token; subsequent generation is fast.

Draft rollout plan:
- Week 0–2: internal prototype + unit tests (serving-runtime branch + local memstore).
- Week 3–5: integrate API + telemetry + basic Console visibility for team-only.
- Week 6–10: internal pilots + iterate on representation and TTL heuristics.
- Post-pilot: documentation + public beta for hosted customers, opt-in for Dedicated/Private.

Notes to self (quick):
- run 'kv-delta-diff' bench against gpt-like-7b / redwood-llm-13b; collect size distribution.
- check with legal on default retention + PII redaction language.
- sync with Console team about snapshot listing UX (Jonah).

Rough acceptance checklist for MVP (to convert to JIRA tasks):
- [ ] in-memory snapshot store + API endpoints
- [ ] capture unit tests for fidelity (decode parity tests)
- [ ] auto-snapshot heuristic implemented behind flag
- [ ] telemetry events emitted and visible in Console
- [ ] GC policy + TTL enforcement
- [ ] pilot run with 3 customers and written report

Random brainstorm / fringe ideas (parking lot):
- composable snapshots: store multiple small anchors (system prompt anchor, last-turn anchor) and allow partial restores (only last-turn anchor) for ultra-fast resumes.
- collaborative snapshots: share snapshot link across devices for multi-client handoff (careful with auth).
- token-aware billing: restore call bundles a small fixed fee + meter token usage after restore.

-- end scratchpad --
